messages.content: You are a fluent, native English-speaking member of this community: AO3 作品评论区.

Readers: 写这篇同人的作者. What the writer wants to do: 称赞人物刻画，并追问布洛克尾的悔意与感激.
A learner's draft:
<<<
Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you,” Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?

Great work! Kudo attached~
>>>
Work in two steps.
Step 1. Under "### POINTS", list every point the draft makes, in order, as short plain English notes: what is meant, never how it is said. Do not reuse the draft's wording, images or set phrases: note an image, joke or idiom as what it stands for (and that it is playful), so the post can be rewritten without it. Include feelings, jokes and questions. Where something is in another language or unclear, note your best guess of the point.
Step 2. Under "### FRESH", close the draft and write the post from your notes alone, as you would write it yourself for these readers: your own sentence shapes, emphasis, idioms and rhythm. Keep every point, the writer's register and tone markers (emoji, "lol", "~"), a similar length, and their order unless another order clearly serves the reader better.
Reply with the two sections only.

result.text:
### POINTS

1. The writer praises the inner monologue of Brokenstar (called "Brokentail" once, which is the same cat). It shows how he used his clanmates to get ahead and power, and how he trained himself to ignore and distrust every kindness shown to him.
2. It makes sense to the writer that he would decide fear and force are the only real way to earn respect, and that he would insist this was the only correct path.
3. The writer appreciates the effort put into the scenes between Yellowfang and her son in his final days. These scenes add depth to her complicated relationship with him.
4. The writer finds the alternate ending, which departs from canon, more emotionally powerful than the original.
5. The writer quotes his line from the fic, "This is more than I deserve from you," and asks about it.
6. The writer asks whether he accepts his fate because of his sense of duty as a leader, which the writer put in quotation marks as if it were a phrase from the fic.
7. The writer asks whether he has come to accept Yellowfang as his mother and feels grateful for her care at the end. The writer also asks whether he feels any regret for how he treated her.
8. Closing: the writer says the work is great and that they left kudos. The tone is friendly and warm, with a tilde marking the playful ending.

### FRESH

Wow... the way you wrote Brokenstar's inner thoughts really shows how he used everyone around him to climb higher, and how he slowly trained himself to brush off every bit of kindness and never trust any of it. It makes total sense that he'd land on fear and force as the only way to get respect, and that he'd dig in and insist that was the one right way to do things.

The work you put into the Yellowfang scenes in his last days gives so much more weight to her messy, complicated bond with her son. And the alternate ending hit me harder emotionally than canon did. "This is more than I deserve from you"... did he accept his fate because he still felt he had to act like a leader to the end? And he also seems to see her as his mother now and feel grateful for her care at the very end. Was there even a little regret for what he did to her? Asking because I'm still thinking about it lol

Great work! Kudos left~
